$comment: Cue D of the score. Machinery, not glory.
title: Iron and Rails

musical.notes: The one cue that must never sound like a victory march: the forts fall, and the point is the machinery, not the glory. Takes the ritardando at the end of cue C and turns settling gears into the first rail joint.

provenance.prompt: Instrumental underscore, 72 BPM, D minor. The iron rhythm of rail joints in bowed double basses and low piano. Horn clusters swell and recede without resolving. A bass drum felt rather than heard, like artillery beyond the horizon. Massive but restrained, no fanfare, no triumph, no snare. Relentless and unbroken, machinery indifferent to what it is carrying.
provenance.excludes: snare drum, military march, fanfare, triumphant, heroic, vocals, choir, epic trailer, taiko
